summary: IdP claim rename causes service-proxy session validation failures for internal analytics portal
description:
Summary: Multiple employees report immediate 401/403 when accessing the internal analytics portal web UI and CLI flows after a planned OKTA profile attribute rename rollover. The IdP attribute 'departmentCode' was renamed to 'dept_code' in a scheduled change; some downstream components reject sessions that contain the old claim name.

Background: We rolled a non-breaking claim mapping change on 2026-03-09 at 03:00 UTC intended to standardize claim names across services. Most services were updated in the mapping table, but the identity-proxy service still validates session cookies by expecting the legacy claim name. This results in signature validation success but claim parsing fails and the proxy returns 401 for affected users.
impact: ~120 unique sign-ins across SSO tracked as failures in last 6 hours. Several oncall engineers and product users cannot access analytics dashboards; internal scheduled jobs that fetch metrics via the internal-cli are failing. Potentially blocks incident response and data analysis during business hours.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a user account with Okta profile that had departmentCode populated. 2) Authenticate via SSO into console.redwood.internal. 3) Observe redirect to analytics-portal and 401 from identity-proxy; CLI login flows (redwood-cli auth login) return 'session validation failed: missing required claim' error. 4) Capture auth header and inspect JWT claims: old claim name present in some tokens, new claim name in others.
logs:
identity-proxy.log excerpt (2026-03-10T09:12:34Z): "ERROR session_validation: missing expected claim 'dept_code' for user jdoe@redwood.com; raw_claims: {"departmentCode":"ENG-2"}"
analytics-portal nginx access: 401 responses correlated to requests with cookie session_id=xxxx.
Auth service issued tokens: some tokens include both claims for a short transitional window; others only include departmentCode. No token signature errors.
investigation_notes: - Confirmed Okta mapping change executed at 2026-03-09 03:00 UTC. - Deployment inventories show identity-proxy config not updated during the rollout (stale config entry). - Proxy code defensively validates presence of 'dept_code' only; it treats missing claim as authentication error. - Edge case: tokens minted by older auth cache include 'departmentCode' only; new mint includes 'dept_code'. - Hypothesis: staggered rollout and a long-lived auth-cache produced mixed tokens leading to validation failures. - Quick check: restarting identity-proxy with updated mapping fixes parsing for web logins but some CLI tokens remain rejected due to token caching at CLI gateway layer.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:30 - Liam O'Connor: Noting that identity-proxy config set still had legacy mapping. Will apply hotfix and reload proxy.
2026-03-10 09:42 - SRE (Priya Mehta): Rolling restart planned for us-east identity-proxy cluster at 10:00 UTC. Coordinating with auth-cache eviction to avoid mixed token population.
2026-03-10 10:05 - Support (Ethan Miller): Customer-facing impact internal only; notified #internal-support channel and paused scheduled analytics jobs.
2026-03-12 16:20 - Liam O'Connor: Follow-up - identified two service accounts that still sign tokens with legacy claim due to pinned library version. Created PRs to patch and added to rollout list.
workarounds: - Short term: restart identity-proxy nodes to accept legacy claim name (degraded but restores access). - Evict auth-cache entries for tokens minted before mapping change. - Instruct CLI users to run 'redwood-cli auth logout' and re-login to get fresh tokens.
resolution: In Progress: Patch landed to accept either claim name in parsing layer (PR https://github.com/redwood/auth-proxy/pull/1102). Staggered rollout completed in us-east and us-west clusters on 2026-03-12 15:30 UTC. Remaining work: patch legacy signer library in two internal token-issuing service accounts (PR open), and add a postmortem documenting rollout checklist to avoid service config skew.
next_steps: 1) Merge and deploy signer-library patches (owners: @infra-team). 2) Run global auth-cache eviction job and monitor 401 rates for 48 hours. 3) Add pre-rollout verification step ensuring all proxies have updated mapping. 4) Publish a short runbook for claim rename operations.
